correctness.rationale: In the repaired counting claim, any path uses at most two arms; the leaf-to-leaf path across the two fullest arms attains their count sum. The admissible count patterns split disjointly into all counts ≤1, one doubled arm with remaining counts ≤1, or one tripled arm alone. In the all-unit case the full set is the unique facet. Otherwise a face of the first type extends by filling an empty arm or doubling an arm; a doubled arm extends exactly when another arm is still vacant, and a tripled arm never extends. This gives the stated polynomials and purity criterion, including d=2 where the families can have the same size. With one length-three arm and arbitrarily many unit arms both sizes occur, differing by d−2. The repaired attribution is also correct: in the prior Morse complex the only within-arm forbidden pairs are x_i y_i, y_i z_i, z_i w_i, and the cross-arm ones are x_i x_j. Replacing y_i by w_i never causes a forbidden pair, even in the union of a face and its image, so the equivariant retraction is contiguous to the identity after inclusion. The retained complex is the stellar subdivision of each doubled-arm edge of the two-edge-arm complex, equivariantly, with new midpoint x_i; no face contains two doubled arms. This transfers the prior integral module, not just its character.
residual_risks: The universal proof is combinatorial; finite checker evidence is supplementary and was not executed.

value.rationale: The repaired result treats the first threshold beyond ordinary edge general position in the basic multiarm tree model. It addresses all inclusion-maximal choices, not just a maximum, and pinpoints exactly when a saturated one-arm choice is arbitrarily smaller than a saturated multiarm choice. The exact arm-length-sensitive size polynomials and purity criterion are usable in comparisons of geodesically constrained set complexes; no value is attributed to recomputing the known topological invariant.
residual_risks: No general-tree, general-threshold, or new topological theorem is asserted.
